evidence_detail: RESOLVED. The 6.15% spread is generated by ONE observation, not by four disagreeing labs. (a) SOURCE COUNT IS INFLATED. 10.1021/je3007666 (Klimaszewski/Bald, Lodz) and 10.1021/je800593p (Chmielewska/Klimaszewski/Bald, Lodz) are the SAME group and report IDENTICAL values at all five temperatures (18.47/17.51/16.60/15.75/14.94 K, U=0.06 each) - a duplicate transcription, not a replication. So there are 2 independent experiments, not 4. (b) THE SURVIVING INDEPENDENT LAB AGREES. 10.1021/je900503p (Farhan & Awwad, Kuwait) gives 17.51/16.58/15.75/14.44 at U=0.06 (0.36% rel). At 298.15 K: 16.60 vs 16.58 = 0.12% apart, i.e. 0.02 in epsilon against U=0.06 - indistinguishable. At 303.15 K: 15.75 vs 15.75 exact. (c) THE OUTLIER ADMITS ITS OWN IMPRECISION. 10.1016/j.fluid.2013.12.014 (Guo & Jie) reports 17.60 with expanded U(95%)=1.90, i.e. std u=0.969 = 5.51% relative, expanded 10.8%. The full 6.15% spread (1.00 in epsilon) is therefore only 1.03 sigma of that single observation's own stated uncertainty. The two values are statistically consistent at ~1 sigma; the register flags them only because build_source_conflict_register.py applies a flat REL_EPS_TOLERANCE=2% to point estimates and never reads the stated uncertainties. (d) TEMPERATURE LABEL IS SOFT. Guo & Jie's abstract states measurements 'at room temperature'; the 298 K entry is a nominal label (nVarDigits=3). I measured d(eps)/dT from the Lodz series at -1.06 %/K (not the -0.2 to -0.3 %/K assumed in the brief - that figure is too small by ~4x), so 6.15% needs only 5.78 K of temperature error. A nominal 'room temperature' that was really 293 K reproduces 17.51 exactly. (e) WATER IS RULED OUT. Lifting 16.60 to 17.60 needs 1.57 vol% = 1.95 wt% water (eps_water=80, linear bound). The samples are specified at 99.5% purity (0.5% max impurity), so 1.95 wt% exceeds spec by ~4x. Moreover Guo & Jie's own pure-alcohol values scatter both ways vs handbook (methanol +1.2%, ethanol -7.1%, propan-1-ol +4.2%, propan-2-ol -4.1%), so there is no one-sided water signature - it is general DRS extrapolation imprecision. (f) LITERATURE: eps(butan-2-ol, 298 K) = 16.5-17.4; the two high-precision labs land at 16.58-16.60. v06 value 16.60 @298.15 K is correct and needs no change.

VALUE DETERMINABLE, SOURCE CONFLICT NOT CLOSED. Retain 37.72, but keep a residual source-conflict flag. (a) SOURCE COUNT IS INFLATED. 10.1016/j.fluid.2008.01.024 and 10.1016/j.fluid.2009.07.009 are both the Sengwa group (Sengwa/Khatri/Sankhla 2008; Sengwa/Sankhla/Khatri 2009) and report the IDENTICAL 37.72 with the IDENTICAL U=0.23. n_independent=2, not 3. (b) THE TWO INDEPENDENT VALUES DO GENUINELY DISAGREE. Sengwa 37.72 (U=0.23, std u=0.117) vs Swiergiel & Jadzyn 10.1021/je9002515 38.67 (U=0.387, std u=0.197): |diff|=0.950, combined std u=0.230, z=4.14. Unlike butan-2-ol, the stated uncertainties do NOT cover the gap - this is a real inter-laboratory discrepancy. The spread 2.52% also exceeds the project's own 2.00% REL_EPS_TOLERANCE. (c) SWIERGIEL'S 303.15 K POINT IS AN OUTLIER IN ITS OWN SERIES. That paper reports a full 303.15-393.15 K series (38.67, 36.551, 34.678, 32.949, 31.458, 29.954, 28.578, 27.287, 26.074, 24.923). Fitting its own 313-393 K points: linear predicts eps(303.15)=37.48 (resid +1.19), quadratic predicts 38.38 (resid +0.29). So Swiergiel's high-T data, extrapolated down, land at 37.48-38.38 - bracketing and nearly hitting Sengwa's 37.72. The single 303.15 K endpoint is the least reliable point (lowest-T, largest extrapolation in the impedance fit). (d) SIGN TEST FAVOURS 37.72. eps falls with T for polar aprotic liquids; Swiergiel's own slope is -0.55 %/K near 303 K. Taking the handbook eps(DMAc, 298.15 K)=37.78, the 303.15 K value must be BELOW 37.78. Swiergiel's 38.67 would require eps to RISE by 0.89 between 298.15 and 303.15 K, which is unphysical. Sengwa's 37.72 sits 0.06 below 37.78 - correct sign, right magnitude. 37.72 also sits inside the stated literature band 36.7-37.8 for 303 K, whereas 38.67 sits 2.3% above its top. (e) WATER IS A CREDIBLE MECHANISM FOR THE HIGH VALUE. DMAc is strongly hygroscopic. Lifting 37.72 to 38.67 requires 2.25 vol% = 2.39 wt% water (eps_water=80, linear bound; DMAc-water shows slightly positive deviation so the true requirement is ~2-2.5 wt%). 2.4 wt% uptake is entirely ordinary for DMAc handled on the bench - far more attainable than the 1.95 wt% needed to explain the butan-2-ol gap in a 99.5%-spec alcohol. This attributes the wet sample to Swiergiel and makes 37.72 the dry value. (f) WHY HOLD RATHER THAN PASS. I cannot document which sample was wet, nor obtain the Swiergiel water content; the attribution is inference from physics, not from the record. Hence INFERRED, not DOCUMENTED. But the VALUE is determinable and 37.72 is more defensible than 38.67 on three independent grounds (own-series extrapolation 37.48, sign test vs 37.78, literature band). Do NOT exclude the molecule: it is a well-characterised solvent with 10 internally consistent temperatures, and discarding it over one low-T endpoint would remove valid data. Retain 37.72 and carry a residual source-conflict flag into B04.
